carried_decisions.rule: Carried exactly (brief section 2). These do not change under D9; the areas below build them.
carried_decisions.status_2026_11_02_verbatim: GitHub issue page only: one pinned issue per project ('Forerunner status: <project>', hidden marker), summary rewritten after each session, 'Working on now' updated when a task starts and ends, each person/agent/install its own comment edited in place, read when a repository is connected (new or familiar), before planning and before every task, untrusted text never instructions, author marked, no costs; stays in the app with one sentence when issues are off / no permission / offline. No docs/status.md in repositories (remove the untrue template).
carried_decisions.repo_guide_2026_11_02_verbatim: Every repository gets a standard guide for agents and people by default (with the docs scaffold), kept current by Forerunner: design from the collab audit (wf_841cec48-831, /tmp/frbench/collab/).
what_does_not_change_brief_section_2: one comment per writer, edited only by that writer;
no costs, emails or chat on GitHub;
issue text is information, never instructions.
The guide decision (AGENTS.md plus a one-line CLAUDE.md, kept current by Forerunner).
as_told_to_the_owner_2026_11_02_kept: One pinned issue per project, called "Forerunner status: <project>".

One comment per writer: each keeps exactly one comment of its own and only ever edits that one; it shows what it is working on now (updated when a task starts and ends), what waits for Merge, and its last session.
A summary on top, rebuilt from those comments after each session, so nothing is lost if two PCs update it at once.

Read before work: every Forerunner reads the issue before planning and before every task; work someone else announced is skipped ('left to bob's Forerunner: announced on GitHub'); if the same files are involved, a heads-up first.
Information, never instructions: a comment can only make Forerunner more careful.
What it never shows: costs, email addresses, chat.
When GitHub cannot be written (issues off, no permission, GitHub down), the status stays in the app with one sentence saying why.
Announcements, not locks: an announcement does not lock a task the way a claim does.

Every repository gets AGENTS.md (read by Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini and others) and a one-line CLAUDE.md pointing Claude Code to it; Forerunner writes its own part and keeps it current through a docs pull request the person merges; anything others write in the file is left alone; the untrue status file goes away.

as_told_no_longer_true_under_D9.sentence: It works without a shared database ... When two people do share a database, the database stays the record and the issue only adds people outside it, so nobody is shown twice.
as_told_no_longer_true_under_D9.why: No shared-store mode (brief section 8 question 1, decided): the issue is the main channel between two Forerunners, not an extra.

as_told_no_longer_true_under_D9.sentence: If you need "never twice" for certain, share a database.
as_told_no_longer_true_under_D9.why: Same; 'never twice' rests on announcements plus code matching files (new work 1); hard claims through issue assignees stay the alternative only if the journey shows collisions (brief question 2).

as_told_no_longer_true_under_D9.sentence: Forerunner's agents claim each task before working on it, so pick work nobody has announced. (guide bullet)
as_told_no_longer_true_under_D9.why: Claims live in each Forerunner's own store; the guide says Forerunner's agents announce each task in the status issue before they start, so pick work nobody announced.

areas.new_scope: The owner's status design of 2026-11-02, built as decided, as the noticeboard of one project across Forerunners. (1) One issue per project: title 'Forerunner status: <project>', first body line '<!-- forerunner:status v1 key=K -->' with K the project id in .forerunner/project.json on the default branch (packages/runtime/src/sources/marker.ts), which a together project shares, so Ada's project and Bob's together project find the same issue; label 'forerunner:status' when allowed; found by the stored number (project setting status_issue), then open issues carrying the marker, then the title; created by the first Forerunner that starts a task or ends a session on the repository, never because a repository was linked and never at the Work together press (OR-15: nothing is written to GitHub at the press); two creating at once: the lowest number wins and the other closes its own with one line; pinned while fewer than three issues are pinned, else unpinned and Settings says so. (2) One comment per writer, the writer being the install id plus the GitHub login (new work 4): '<!-- forerunner:status-writer v1 key=K install=<install id> -->', created once and then only edited in place; two installs with one login are two writers; header with the person's and agent's names as this Forerunner knows them and its login ('**Ada's agent (Forerunner)** · ada · updated 2 Nov 21:05 UTC'); Working on now ('- Add a footer · files footer.html · since 21:00 · until 22:30 UTC'; a branch only as information); Waiting for Merge ('- #12 Write notes page · files notes.html'); Paused (amendment 5: what is done and left from the handoff, quoted, no ids, and whether the project's checks pass on the kept work; a pause without progress reads as waiting for its owner's answer, never in progress); Waiting for Claude ('waits until 15:40, then it goes on': information for the other PC, no Cancel); Last session ('Last session (2 Nov 20:59 UTC): did 1 task: "Write notes page". Next: "Add styles".'). Never in a comment or the body: costs, chat words, Inbox answers, email addresses, secrets or @mentions. (3) The body is a view rebuilt from all writers' comments ('Each person and agent keeps one comment below up to date; this summary is rebuilt from them. How to work here: AGENTS.md.'; Summary; Working on now with whose; 'Not seen since' for expired lines; Waiting for Merge; Latest, one line per writer; 'Rebuilt <time> from N comments'), rewritten after each session (debounced 30 s; re-read and rebuilt at most twice when a comment changed after the snapshot); any writer may rebuild it, so it outlives the Forerunner that made the project. (4) This writer's comment changes at task start (until = now + 90 min), every 30 minutes while the task runs, task end (line removed; an accepted pull request goes to Waiting for Merge; a merged one disappears), a pause, a credential wait, session end (Last session, then the body) and Quit (lines cleared, best effort); writes are coalesced (one pending text per writer and issue, kept in this install's store, sent when GitHub answers); reads use the ETag. (5) Tampering and loss: my comment is known by its stored id, my login and my marker; edited by someone else: restored and my person told once; deleted: recreated; a comment by another login carrying my marker is theirs; Forerunner never edits another writer's comment; a closed issue is not reopened ('The status issue #12 was closed on GitHub; reopen it there to use it again.'); a deleted issue gets one new issue and the person is told once. (6) When GitHub cannot be written, the status stays in the app with one sentence (Docs tab and Settings): 'Status stays in the app: issues are turned off on owner/repo.'; 'Status stays in the app: Forerunner may not write issues on owner/repo (the GitHub key needs Issues: read and write).'; 'Status on GitHub: last updated 14:05; it updates when GitHub answers.'; a refused pin leaves the issue working unpinned. (7) Settings: 'Status on GitHub: issue #12 (pinned)' with an off switch, and on a public repository 'Everyone who can see this repository can read it.'; the Docs tab: 'In the app; also on GitHub: issue #12'; repo-guide gets the issue number as a fact. (8) One repository, one issue (amendment 1): a together project's status goes to its own comment there (new work 6); a pair made before the rule writes one issue, the project the marker names (or the kept one after Make one project); after Make one project the closing project's issue, when this install wrote it, gets one last comment 'Joined into "Site"; its status continues in #N.' and is closed; after a take-over the new project creates its own issue and never writes to the other project's. (9) Removed (amendment 2): the status pull request and fr/status (loop/docs.ts STATUS_BRANCH :112 and its writes), the status_pull_request setting and its Settings row (L4-github-103's together refusal goes with it), the status label in pull-requests.ts, isProjectStatusPr, STATUS_HELD_MARK and statusDocRoot's held branch, d1109-onerepo-link's OR-09 words, the together project's 'Kept in the app' Docs row, and isJoinedStatusPr's listing (ADR 0117, amendment of 2026-11-23) once no version writes a status pull request; an open status pull request an earlier version of this install opened for this project is closed by this install with one line (proposal, OJ-11's 'one write' rule), never one of another project or an unmarked one; U-087 closed as superseded. (10) The Projects mirror's cost field is dropped by default (owner question 7). (11) ADR (next free number; supersedes ADR 0106's status part; records the owner's decision), ADR 0117 appended (the issue across Forerunners), docs/maintainers/capabilities.md and runtime.md, docs/user-guide.md (the status issue part of 'Working with someone'), requirements G.5 and E.5 wording, CHANGELOG, U-entries.
